clue.text: Sporting event seen in spring more than once

definitions.text: Sporting event seen in spring more than once

parts.words: Sporting event seen in spring more than once
parts.note: an athletics event in which the competitor springs off the ground three times in a row: hop, step and leap

explanation.surface: Some sports fixture turns up every spring, year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, giving an event held annually; it is really a leap, and 'more than once' means three of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This athletics field event consists of three consecutive bounds, so it is literally springing more than once.

clue.text: Tense runner seeing part of boar

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the Usk is a river in Wales, and a river is a runner

explanation.surface: An anxious athlete spots a wild pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is the River Usk in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A long protruding tooth is a feature of a wild pig's mouth.

clue.text: Ambiguous soundbite endlessly dissected

indicators.note: dissected means cut up and reassembled in another order
endlessly drops the first and last letters of soundbite

explanation.surface: An unclear soundbite has been picked apart without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves OUNDBIT, which 'dissected' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ambiguous leaves one uncertain, unsure what is meant.

clue.text: Extensive calculating needed to create pine border

parts.note: to long is to pine for something
a division is a dividing line or border

explanation.surface: A lot of working out goes into making a pine edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like timber, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing big numbers on paper, step by step, is a lengthy arithmetic method.

clue.text: Can investor become a symbol of Britain?

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
a bull is an investor who expects prices to rise

explanation.surface: Could an investor end up as a national emblem?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb; it is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The stout, waistcoated cartoon Englishman personifies the nation, as Uncle Sam does the USA.

clue.text: Horse charity disturbs soldiers

indicators.note: disturbs says the charity breaks into the soldiers word

parts.note: men are soldiers, the ranks
aid is charity, help given

explanation.surface: A horse-welfare charity upsets the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like part of the charity's name; it is the definition, a racing term.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse that has never won a race is called by this term.

clue.text: Backing increased in very good musical piece

indicators.note: Backing means the whole assembled string is read from the end towards the start
in says one word sits inside the other

parts.note: so means very, as in so kind
up means increased, as in prices are up

explanation.surface: Support grew for a fine piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns the whole container round, not just one piece; 'good' belongs to the definition, a notable work.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbered composition, especially a notable one, is a standard term for a work of music.

clue.text: Perhaps tablet computer winning the European award's revolutionary

indicators.note: winning means the computer gains, and so contains, the next piece

parts.note: PC is a personal computer
la is the in French, a European language

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the award is read backwards

parts.note: OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A tablet computer that wins a European prize is said to be ground-breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps tablet' looks like it means a device; it is a pill. 'revolutionary' turns OBE to EBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given with no active drug, as in trials, is an example of a tablet.

clue.text: Wading birds attracted to circular geranium-like flower

parts.note: storks are long-legged wading birds
a bill is a printed notice, a circular

explanation.surface: Waders are drawn to a round flower resembling a geranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular' looks like an adjective for the flower; it is a noun, a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: Erodium plants, cousins of cranesbills, are named for their long beaked fruit.

clue.text: Transport journeys returning include one cuppa?

indicators.note: include says the reversed word takes the other pieces inside it
returning means the word for journeys is read backwards

parts.note: rides are journeys on a horse or vehicle
an means one, the indefinite article
cha is slang for tea, a cuppa

explanation.surface: Coming home from trips, you stop for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British slang for tea; 'Transport' is a carried seat, not a modern vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered seat carried on poles by two bearers was a form of conveyance for one passenger.

clue.text: Flipping, some do catch pancake

indicators.note: Flipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tossing pancakes, some of them get caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Flipping' fits a pancake surface but turns OCAT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla, a flat round of maize bread, is loosely a pancake folded round a filling.

clue.text: Swimmer barely sees captain around pub with yard

indicators.note: around says the captain word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a skipper is a ship's captain
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A swimmer barely makes out the captain near a pub with a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean hardly; it means naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bathing naked swims bare, so the definition is a punning description.

clue.text: Ageing Glaswegian oddly rejected casual dress at first

indicators.note: oddly rejected means the first, third and fifth letters of casual are thrown away, keeping the even ones
at first takes the opening letter of dress

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Glasgow turned down casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly rejected' drops C, S, A from 'casual', leaving AUL; 'at first' supplies D.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect, spoken in Glasgow, uses this word for old, as in the New Year song.

clue.text: After opening, drink scarily fast

indicators.note: After says the drink word follows the opening word

parts.note: a break is an opening or gap
to neck is to drink quickly, British slang

explanation.surface: Once the bottle is opened, someone gulps it down alarmingly quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'neck' a drink is British slang for swallowing it fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed that risks a broken neck is dangerously, frighteningly rapid.

clue.text: Sheets of paper spread round engrossed in Shakespeare

parts.note: paste is a spread, as on bread

indicators.note: engrossed in means the round letter is absorbed into the poet's title

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Pages spread round by someone absorbed in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff board made by gluing paper sheets together is a material from layered paper.

clue.text: See appended part of play with animation

indicators.note: appended says the See word is tacked onto the end

parts.note: Act IV is a section of a play
Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a scene added to a theatrical script.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with animation means doing it energetically and in a lively way.

clue.text: Plant bent in a storm around middle of Cromer

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the other piece
in a storm suggests letters blown about and rearranged
middle of takes the central letters of Cromer

explanation.surface: A plant is bent over in a gale near the Norfolk town of Cromer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is the verb, to bury; Cromer is a seaside town in Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant a body is to bury it, to lay it in a grave.

clue.text: Boast coming from first-class in aeroplane departing

indicators.note: in says the class letter sits inside the aeroplane

parts.note: the Moth was a de Havilland light aeroplane
U means upper class, the top class
off means departing, as in they're off

explanation.surface: Bragging from the first-class cabin as the plane takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the convention for upper-class or posh; the de Havilland Moth was a classic small biplane.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk loudly and brashly, showing off, is a colloquial verb for bragging.

clue.text: Drive Triumph, disheartened by corrosion

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart of Triumph is removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Someone drives a Triumph car and is dismayed to find it rusting.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumph is a classic British car make, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and push both mean a forceful forward impetus or main point of an argument.

clue.text: Observer's section covers Southern wine

indicators.note: covers says the eye part wraps round the other letter

parts.note: the retina is a part of an observer's eye

explanation.surface: A part of the Observer newspaper reviews wine from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer's section' suggests a newspaper supplement; it is a part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek white flavoured with pine resin is a specific type of wine.

clue.text: Hairstyle 25 pounds — join queue

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling
to tail is to follow on behind, joining the back of a line

explanation.surface: A haircut costs twenty-five pounds, so get in line.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pony' is British slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair gathered at the back and tied so it hangs down is a familiar style.

clue.text: Lots here from university involved in lawsuit

indicators.note: involved in says the university letter is wrapped inside the lawsuit

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Plenty of business here from a university caught up in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' reads as many; it means items numbered for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbered items called lots are sold to bidders at a public sale, so this is where they appear.

clue.text: Scoff at quiet centre of wood repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the built piece occurs twice

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letters of wood

explanation.surface: Mocking the silence deep in the woods again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives OO from WOOD, after P from piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something contemptuously is to deride or scorn it.

clue.text: Reach lowest point with repellent slogan during fight

indicators.note: during says the slogan sits inside the fight word

parts.note: a bout is a boxing fight

indicators.note: repellent, pushing back, says the slogan word is turned backwards

parts.note: a motto is a slogan

explanation.surface: Hitting rock bottom with a nasty catchphrase in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repellent' looks like an adjective describing the slogan; here it means pushing back, a turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A market or recession is said to flatten out at its lowest level before recovering.

clue.text: Burning pine

definitions.meaning: burning as an adjective in the sense of an eager urge, as in a burning desire
to pine is to long for something

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a restless craving: a skin sensation one wants relieved, and a strong yearning to do something.

clue.text: Complaint made using pen name at the end

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: at the end takes the last letter of name

explanation.surface: A grievance written under a pseudonym, signed at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is a medical one, not a grievance; 'pen name' falsely joins two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is a minor ailment, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Ford reversed in close

indicators.note: reversed means the car model name is read backwards

parts.note: the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: A Ford car is backed into a close, a cul-de-sac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like a dead-end street, but it is the adjective meaning related.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things closely related or similar are said to be alike or kindred.

clue.text: Partly capable of having some beer, getting round in

parts.note: up to means capable of, as in up to the job

indicators.note: in says the round letter is put into the beer phrase

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
getting round gives O, the round letter, a ring shape

explanation.surface: Capable of having a beer, and offering to get a round in.
explanation.walkthrough: In pub talk a round is drinks bought for the whole group, but here it is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing to a limited extent, not wholly, is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Seaside town traffic

definitions.meaning: a coastal town in Kent, England
to traffic is to trade or do business

explanation.definitionFit: The Kent resort shares its name with the verb for trading or bargaining, as in dealing in goods.

clue.text: Meeting party joins monarch inside barrier

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, a political party

indicators.note: inside says the monarch sits within the barrier

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Political party joins the Queen behind a barrier for talks.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Latin cipher of Queen Elizabeth; CON abbreviates Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal gathering for discussion, such as a party's annual one, is a synonym for meeting.
